title: Why Do Hamster Cheeks Stretch Almost 3x? 🐹
description:
Why do hamsters stuff food in their cheeks? Their stretchy cheek pouches run all the way back to the shoulders and can nearly triple in size, so wild hamsters can carry food home to an underground pantry and push it out with their front paws.

Sources:
https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/article/cheek-pouches-stuffed-animals-news
https://www.chewy.com/education/small-pet/hamster/hamsters-fun-facts

topic: Why do hamsters stuff food in their cheeks?
script: Your hamster hides two secret pockets that nearly triple in size. Why? Inside each cheek is a long stretchy pouch, a dead-end sleeve that runs all the way back to the shoulders. Stuffed full, it balloons out like a backpack. Some hamsters fit a whole baby carrot in there. Wild hamsters live where food is scarce and the weather's harsh. So they don't eat on the spot. They fill up fast, run home, and stash it all in an underground pantry. To unload, they push from the back with their front paws, and out it all pours. A special muscle pulls the empty pouch back in. And here's a bonus: some puff their pouches with air to float when they swim. So if you had two secret pockets, what would you carry home first?
key_facts: Hamster cheek pouches start at the cheek and can extend across the shoulders (National Geographic; Chewy, Dr. Campbell)
Pouches are extremely elastic, expanding to nearly triple their size; Syrian hamsters can fit whole baby carrots (National Geographic)
Pouches are dead-end sleeves of the mouth lining, retracted by a muscle that evolved from the trapezius (Chewy)
Hamsters empty pouches by pushing the contents forward with their paws (Chewy)
Wild hamsters carry food back to underground storage chambers (PBS Nature); elastic pouches tied to cold climate and harsh terrain where food storage matters (National Geographic)
Hamsters can inflate their cheek pouches with air to help them float when swimming (Chewy; Dictionary.com)
